title: Bedside Assessment of The Airway in Resuscitation

notes.text: Airway assessment and patency
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Tongue displacement can obstruct the upper airway in an unconscious person.
Jaw thrust can help open the airway when cervical motion should be minimized.
Oropharyngeal airways are generally used only when the gag reflex is absent.
Oxygenation and ventilation must both be assessed because a patent airway alone does not guarantee adequate gas exchange.

title: Scaphoid Fractures: Herbert Classification, Imaging, Clinical Features, Treatment and Complications

notes.text: Scaphoid fracture essentials
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Anatomic snuffbox tenderness after a fall on an outstretched hand raises suspicion of scaphoid injury.
Initial radiographs may be normal despite a fracture.
Retrograde blood supply makes proximal scaphoid injuries vulnerable to avascular necrosis.
Nonunion is an important complication of missed or unstable fractures.

title: Wrist Injuries: Normal Anatomy, Sprains, TFCC tears and X ray imaging

notes.text: Wrist anatomy and injury
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Distal radioulnar joint stability supports forearm pronation and supination.
Triangular fibrocartilage complex injuries can cause ulnar-sided wrist pain.
Scapholunate ligament disruption can alter carpal alignment.
Neurovascular assessment is part of evaluating any significant wrist injury.

title: Hepatic Encephalopathy: Pathophysiology, Clinical Features, Diagnosis & Treatment

notes.text: Hepatic encephalopathy
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Hepatic encephalopathy is brain dysfunction associated with liver insufficiency or portosystemic shunting.
Asterixis is a possible examination finding but is not specific to this condition.
Precipitating factors include infection, gastrointestinal bleeding, constipation, and medication effects.
West Haven grading describes clinical severity from subtle changes through coma.

title: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD): Causes, Clinical Features, Classification, Treatment

notes.text: Gastroesophageal reflux
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Lower esophageal sphincter dysfunction permits gastric contents to reflux into the esophagus.
Heartburn and regurgitation are typical symptoms.
Dysphagia is an alarm symptom requiring further assessment.
Barrett esophagus is a metaplastic complication associated with chronic reflux.

title: H. Pylori Treatment: All Treatment Regimens Explained

notes.text: H. pylori treatment principles
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Antibiotic resistance is a key determinant of eradication regimen selection.
Bismuth quadruple therapy is a recommended empiric option in the ACG 2024 guidance when susceptibility is unknown.
Clarithromycin susceptibility should be established before using clarithromycin triple therapy under that guidance.
Test of cure is needed after eradication treatment; symptom relief alone does not prove eradication.

title: Bismuth Subsalicylates: Mechanism of Action, Therapeutic Uses & Adverse Effects

notes.text: Bismuth subsalicylate
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Bismuth contributes local protective and antimicrobial effects in the gastrointestinal tract.
Salicylate exposure is relevant to allergy, interactions, and toxicity risk.
Dark stools and a dark tongue may occur and can be benign medication effects.
Combination therapy uses bismuth as one component of some H. pylori eradication regimens.

title: Therapy for Peptic Ulcer Disease Free Course Introduction

notes.text: Peptic ulcer disease foundations
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
H. pylori infection and NSAID exposure are major causes of peptic ulcer disease.
Muscularis mucosae penetration distinguishes an ulcer from a more superficial erosion.
Gastrointestinal bleeding and perforation are important complications.
Cause-directed treatment combines acid suppression with correction of the underlying driver.

title: Oxygen Therapy: Oxygen Delivery Devices, Indications, Adverse Effects, Monitoring and MORE

notes.text: Oxygen therapy principles
A concise, newly authored revision guide for this topic. Use the video for the instructor’s full explanation; these notes do not claim to transcribe it.
Oxygenation refers to oxygen transfer into blood and is distinct from carbon dioxide clearance.
Pulse oximetry estimates arterial oxygen saturation but does not directly measure ventilation.
Controlled oxygen delivery allows adjustment to the patient’s target and clinical response.
Hypercapnia risk warrants careful monitoring in susceptible patients.
